title: api-config-design-scratchpad-jamie
content:
Personal scratchpad for API + config design (WIP).

Goal:
- Define a simple, flexible API shape for per-route/tenant serving configuration that can express routing policies, quantization preferences, batching hints, and fallbacks. Keep client SDK ergonomics in mind (short, typed shapes).

Constraints / non-goals:
- This is not the full runtime config surface (that lives in infra manifests). Aim for a user-facing declaration that the control plane stores and validates.
- Backwards compatibility: additive changes only; provide defaulting behavior server-side.

Quick sketch of proposed HTTP API (REST):
POST /v1/configs              # create or update config
GET  /v1/configs/{config_id}  # fetch config
GET  /v1/configs?owner=org    # list

Example JSON payload (user-facing):
{
  "id": "marketing-chat-1",
  "owner": "team-marketing",
  "routes": [
    {
      "path": "/chat/generate",
      "priority": 10,
      "model": "redwood/ggml-redwood-7b-q4f16",
      "routing": {
        "preferred_region": "us-west1",
        "fallback_models": ["redwood/opt-2.7b-quant"],
        "tier": "hosted"
      },
      "performance": {
        "max_latency_ms": 250,
        "batching": {
          "enabled": true,
          "max_batch_size": 16,
          "latency_budget_ms": 50
        },
        "kv_cache": {
          "prefetch": true,
          "ttl_seconds": 3600
        }
      },
      "quality": {
        "temperature": 0.2,
        "max_tokens": 512
      },
      "quantization": {
        "preference": "auto",
        "allowed_modes": ["q4f16", "q8_0"],
        "min_quality_score": 0.92
      },
      "observability": {
        "sampling_rate": 0.02,
        "trace_id": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "rollout": {
    "strategy": "canary",
    "canary_percentage": 5,
    "metrics": ["p50_latency_ms", "token_cost_usd", "quality_regression"]
  }
}

Design notes / rationale:
- route-level config lets product teams attach different SLAs/cost-targets per endpoint.
- "quantization.preference=auto" allows platform to pick a quantization mode based on workload and min_quality_score.
- Observability sampling at config-level so we can correlate regressions with config changes.
- Fallbacks are explicit model names; runtime will map to compatible variants.

Open questions / todos:
- How to express multi-model ensembles / reranking (single route vs pipeline of sub-routes)? Need example semantics.
- Do we want top-level "defaults" that routes inherit and can override? Probably yes for ergonomics.
- Should routing.tier be enum [hosted, dedicated, private] or open string? Enum safer.
- How to validate "min_quality_score" across different model families (scale differs). Might need model-family-aware normalization.
- Security: who can set fallback_models? restrict to org admins? put RBAC note.

Quick sketch: YAML variant (shorter for humans)
---
id: marketing-chat-1
owners: [team-marketing]
defaults:
  model: redwood/ggml-redwood-7b-q4f16
  quantization:
    preference: auto
    allowed_modes: [q4f16, q8_0]
routes:
  - path: /chat/generate
    priority: 10
    performance:
      max_latency_ms: 250
      batching:
        enabled: true
        max_batch_size: 16

ASCII diagram of control flow (very rough):

  Client --> Control Plane (validate + store) --> Runtime Router --> [Pool A (hosted), Pool B (dedicated), Private Edge]
                                      |                                 |
                                      v                                 v
                               Observability                          Model KV Cache

Notes about runtime mapping: control plane stores user config; runtime periodically pulls diff (or via push). Router uses policy engine:
- pick pool by routing.tier + preferred_region + capacity health
- select model variant by quantization preference + runtime capability
- apply batching rules per-route and per-model

Integration points / linked tickets:
- INF-4321: config validation work (schema + model-family rules)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/678 (initial config CRUD)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/serving-configs (current state doc)

Small ergonomics ideas for SDKs:
- allow builder pattern: new Config().route(...).batching(...) etc, then .apply()
- allow shorthand: {model: "r/7b", batching: {}} expands to full shape server-side

Testing / rollout plan:
- Start with internal alpha: only org-internal teams can create configs.
- Validate defaulting and backward-compat by importing 10 existing configs from hosted-api.
- Add e2e tests: validate runtime picks fallback model when capacity limited.

Notes-to-self:
- follow up with infra about push vs pull sync (latency vs consistency) - ask @Aisha for infra constraints.
- sketch UI for Console: per-route toggles for batching/kv-cache/observability.

End of scratchpad.

CHANGES LOG (short):
- 2025-01-10: initial draft (Jamie)
- 2025-01-22: added quantization + observability fields (Aisha)
